one_liner: CivicState is a civic-letter prototype, not an investible business until paid demand and inbox trust are proven.
thesis: CivicState can become a narrowly useful civic-action utility if it proves that residents pay for researched, citation-backed letters and officials receive them reliably.
currentEvidence: Repo contains a Next.js submission wizard [evidence: apps/web/app/submit/page.tsx].
Repo contains Express API routes for submissions, officials, payments, webhooks, campaigns, admin, and compliance [evidence: apps/api/src/index.ts].
Repo contains BullMQ workers for classifier, researcher, drafter, delivery, treasury, and reconciliation [evidence: apps/worker/src/index.ts].
Registry dispatch marks this as watchlist and not near-term investible.
killCriteria: Paid beta conversion materially misses 3% target [evidence: .planning/PROJECT.md].
Operator confirms this repo is not the intended brooks-history project.
operatorQuestions: Is brooks-history actually supposed to be CivicState?
Should this be pitched as a business or retained as a personal/research asset?
Who owns legal/compliance review before public official delivery?
